recs.stt: Why I don't spend time with Modern C++ anymore
recs.x:
Of special relevance is the rather excellent talk by Kate Gregory on "Stop Teaching C" (when you're supposed to do an intro course to C++):

"CppCon 2015: Kate Gregory “Stop Teaching C"":
 [link]

I couldn't come up with a better one. I wasn't really talking about the historical relationship between C and C++ but rather about their relative complexities. Learning C++ is vastly more complicated than learning C. On top of that the coding style of a modern C++ application (which generally involves a lot of metaprogramming, OOP and even some functional constructs) is fairly different from a standard C codebase. You don't write C like you write C++ and vice-versa.

There's this good talk about how we should "stop teaching C" (if we want to teach C++): [link]
